summary: Retest of partner Help & Support parity after AppTabBar.hideBarRoutes fix. PRIMARY FIX VERIFIED: on /partner/support/{id} the app-bottom-nav is NO LONGER rendered (count=0), so thread controls are natively clickable (no pointer-event interception). Verified (a) reply: POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/messages -> 200, green own-bubble with time + tick appears; (b) details bottom sheet shows Ticket ID (TKT-100003), Department (Refund), Priority (urgent), Status (Open), Created, Updated, Attachments · 0, Your other tickets · 1; (c) attach-file paperclip is present and enabled; (d) close-ticket has a WEB-SPECIFIC BUG: React Native Alert.alert() does not fire a real confirm dialog on web (react-native-web polyfills to window.alert with no OK callback), so clicking close-ticket does nothing on web — no confirm shown, no /close request, no closed-state UI. Regression: list still shows app-bottom-nav and filters (search/status/sort/range) work; leaving the thread restores the tab bar. NOTE: A frontend supervisor restart was required after the source edits because Metro/web bundler was serving the stale bundle (first test run against the deploy still showed the tab bar); after `supervisorctl restart frontend` the fix rendered correctly.

ui_bugs.issue: Alert.alert('Close ticket?', ..., [Cancel, {text:'Close', onPress: close.mutate}]) does not work on React Native Web. RN Web polyfills Alert.alert as window.alert (single OK button, no callback), so the OK/Close button and its onPress are never rendered on web. Result: tapping [data-testid=close-ticket] produces no confirm and no POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/close is fired. The closed-state UI ('This ticket is closed' composer + centered 'Ticket closed by ...' system message) therefore cannot be reached on the web build.

integration_issues.issue: close.mutate() never called because Alert.alert has no OK callback on RN Web. Use a custom Modal (or Platform.OS === 'web' ? window.confirm(...) : Alert.alert) so the close endpoint fires.

action_items: Replace Alert.alert in confirmClose (app/support/[id].tsx) with a Platform-aware confirm: on web use window.confirm(...) (or a custom in-app <Modal>) so the OK path executes close.mutate() and drives POST /api/support/tickets/{id}/close.

Optional: for future edits to AppTabBar/_layout, remember Metro web can serve a stale bundle — a `sudo supervisorctl restart frontend` may be required to pick up the change (documented for context, not required for main agent action).
critical_code_review_comments: React Native's Alert.alert is not a functional replacement for window.confirm on web — any confirm/destructive flow (close-ticket, delete account, cancel booking, etc.) that relies on the button onPress must be Platform-branched or replaced with an in-app Modal to work on the Expo web build.

hideBarRoutes match in AppTabBar depends on the exact route name registered in the parent Tabs group ('partner/support/[id]'). This is fragile — a rename in the file tree or in _layout.tsx will silently re-introduce the overlap. Consider matching by pathname prefix (usePathname().startsWith('/partner/support/')) as a safety net.

success_rate.frontend: 85% - primary fix works and reply/details/attach verified; only close-ticket confirm broken on web due to Alert.alert polyfill

rca of the issue: Iteration 90 blocker (bottom tab bar overlapping thread composer) is fixed by AppTabBar.hideBarRoutes=['partner/support/[id]'] returning null when active. Confirmed by Playwright: pointer events no longer intercepted, POST /messages fires, own-bubble renders. The residual close-ticket failure is unrelated to layout — it is a React Native Alert.alert incompatibility with react-native-web (polyfilled to single-button window.alert, dropping the second-button onPress), so close.mutate() is never invoked and no /close request is made.
